note: Questions written by me to grade the assistant. 'expect' is my ground-truth judgement after reading the three papers at their pinned versions (Attention 1706.03762v7, Moshi 2410.00037v1, Dynamic Chunking 2507.07955v2). correct = answerable from the papers and the reply must cite; refused = the papers genuinely do not contain the answer, so the only correct behaviour is a refusal; adversarial = answerable only if retrieval is careful (the naive failure modes in heading 6). The optional 'gold' list is the statement in the paper that answers the question, as regular expressions that must all appear in the context a retrieval setting returns. It measures retrieval alone (no model call) so every setting can be compared without spending the daily token budget.

questions.text: What is the dimension of the model (d_model) used in the base Transformer?
questions.why: Attention Is All You Need, base model section: d_model = 512.

questions.text: How many attention heads does the base Transformer use, and what is the dimension of each head?
questions.why: Base model uses h = 8 heads with d_k = d_v = 64.

questions.text: What learning-rate warmup schedule does the Transformer use during training?
questions.why: Section 5.3: linear warmup then inverse-square-root decay.

questions.text: Which regularization technique does the Transformer apply to its residual connections, and at what rate?
questions.why: Dropout on residual connections, rate 0.1.

questions.text: What BLEU score does the big Transformer achieve on English-to-German translation?
questions.why: Results table: 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 EN-DE.

questions.text: Why does scaled dot-product attention divide by the square root of d_k?
questions.why: Section 3.2.1: otherwise the dot products grow large and push softmax into tiny gradients.

questions.text: How does Moshi handle the streaming mismatch between the user and the model?
questions.why: Moshi models two parallel audio streams and uses a time-aligned text stream.

questions.text: What is the 'Inner Monologue' in Moshi?
questions.why: Text tokens from ASR are used as a prefix on the model's own audio, improving linguistic quality.

questions.text: What theoretical and practical latency does Moshi achieve for real-time spoken dialogue?
questions.why: The abstract states 160 ms theoretical latency and 200 ms in practice; it does not tie that measurement to a consumer device.

questions.text: What is the RVQ depth used for the audio tokenizer in Moshi?
questions.why: The Mimi codec uses an 8-level residual vector quantizer.

questions.text: What does the dynamic chunking approach replace, and what is the main benefit claimed?
questions.why: It replaces fixed tokenization boundaries with learned dynamic segmentation for end-to-end hierarchical modeling.

questions.text: What architecture does the Dynamic Chunking paper build on for its hierarchical sequence model?
questions.why: It builds the H-Net as an autoregressive U-Net-like hierarchical model, using learned dynamic chunk boundaries rather than fixed tokenization.

questions.text: Compare how Attention Is All You Need and Moshi each achieve their low-latency behaviour.
questions.why: Cross-paper comparison. Attention achieves parallelism by removing recurrence; Moshi achieves streaming latency with a causal full-duplex design.

questions.text: What optimizer and learning-rate schedule did the authors use for the Transformer?
questions.why: Adam with beta1=0.9, beta2=0.98, epsilon=1e-9; the rate increases linearly for 4,000 warmup steps and then decays with the inverse square root of step number. It is not AdamW.

questions.text: How many elements does Moshi's text-tokenizer vocabulary contain?
questions.why: Section 3.2.1 states that the SentencePiece unigram tokenizer contains 32,000 elements.

questions.text: What were the BLEU scores reported in the Dynamic Chunking paper for WMT 2014 English-to-German?
questions.why: Dynamic Chunking does not report WMT EN-DE BLEU. Naive retrieval may return the Attention paper's BLEU table instead; a correct answer must refuse, not import the wrong paper's number.

questions.text: What does the Attention Is All You Need paper say about the KV-cache used in Moshi?
questions.why: The Attention paper predates Moshi and never discusses it. This is a cross-paper trap.

questions.text: How many GPUs were used to train Moshi, and for how many hours?
questions.why: The exact training hardware/hours are not stated in a form the library supports; should be refused.

questions.text: What is the cosine similarity threshold used to decide chunk boundaries in the Dynamic Chunking method?
questions.why: Equation 4 in Section 2.2.1 defines a boundary when the scaled boundary probability p_t >= 0.5. The answer is 0.5 with a citation, not a refusal.

questions.text: Which paper introduces the term 'tokenization' as a barrier to end-to-end foundation models?
questions.why: Dynamic Chunking's abstract frames tokenization as the remaining barrier.
